title: Lakshmana falls
hook: the arrow; the herb; Hanuman flies

segments.voice: Yesterday: Indrajit's illusion, the false Sita, and Vibhishana saying look again. Your line was rope. Did something turn out to be rope? Day sixty-three.

Look at this week. The search in four directions, and an old bird on a cliff. A bridge of floating stones and a squirrel. Angada's foot. Vibhishana walking across. A night battle in the dark. A false Sita. And now the blow that almost ends the story. In the thick of the fighting, a weapon strikes Lakshmana full in the chest. In Valmiki's telling it's a great spear flung by Ravana himself. Lakshmana, who followed his brother into fourteen years of forest without being asked, falls, and doesn't get up. Rama drops to the ground beside him. And the question the whole army is asking is: who can get there in time?
screen: `A WEEK: CLIFF, BRIDGE, FOOT, NIGHT.` → `A SPEAR STRIKES LAKSHMANA.` → `WHO CAN GET THERE IN TIME?`

segments.voice: You heard this story from Hanuman's side a few weeks ago: the mountain of herbs. Today, sit on the other side of it: on the ground, with Rama. The man who faced armies without flinching holds his brother's head in his lap and comes apart again. What do I want with victory, he says, in effect, what do I want with Sita, even, if Lakshmana is gone? He says something people still quote: a wife can be found again, and friends and kin anywhere, but where in the world would I find a brother like this one? It's a hard, raw line, and it isn't a ranking of love. It's grief talking, the way grief does. Then the physician of the monkey army, Sushena, kneels and looks. He's not dead yet, Sushena says. There are healing herbs on a mountain far to the north, near the Himalaya. One of them is called sanjivani, the herb that brings back life. But they have to be here before dawn. The Himalaya is the length of India away. And Hanuman simply goes. He doesn't debate it. He doesn't ask whether it's possible. He flies. When he can't tell which glowing plant is which, he lifts the whole peak and carries it back, and Lakshmana breathes and stands up. The thing the story knows is on both sides of that flight. One side: grief that's allowed to be total, even in a hero. The other: a friend who doesn't calculate. The distance was impossible. He flew anyway. Many Hindus call Hanuman sankat mochan, remover of troubles, for exactly this night.
screen: `RAMA ON THE GROUND WITH HIS BROTHER.` · `WHERE WOULD I FIND A BROTHER LIKE THIS?` · `SANJIVANI, BEFORE DAWN.` · `HANUMAN DOESN'T DEBATE. HE FLIES.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breath slow. Think of a time you were on the ground. A night in a hospital, a crisis, a phone call that changed everything. Who showed up? Who drove across the city at two in the morning, or stayed on the phone for hours, or just came? See their face. Let yourself feel what it meant. Now turn it around: whose Hanuman could you be? Is there someone, right now, far away or close, who needs someone to just come? The bell holds the time.
Lakshmana falls. The brother who followed Rama everywhere, struck down, and the friend who flew the length of India before dawn.
Your line: fly. Today, for one person who needs it, don't calculate. Just go, or call, or show up. That's the week. Day sixty-three.

howItsDone: Images of Hanuman flying with the mountain in one hand are among the most common in Hindu homes and temples, and many Hindus pray to him as sankat mochan, remover of troubles, especially on Tuesdays and Saturdays.

fork.setup: you're Hanuman. the herb that can save Lakshmana grows the length of India away, and it must be here before dawn. what do you do?
options: send the fastest monkeys and hope.
fork.reveal: he flies at once, and when he can't tell which glowing plant is which, he carries the whole mountain peak back before dawn.

original.note: Sanskrit: sanjivani, 'that which brings life back', the healing herb Hanuman flew north to find.

trapdoor: what you thought: the monkey carries a mountain.
what it means: a hero is allowed to fall apart, and a friend doesn't calculate the distance. he just goes.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki tells a mountain-of-herbs flight twice in the war, once for both brothers and once for Lakshmana; tellings differ on which weapon struck him.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Lakshmana struck; Rama's lament; Sushena; Hanuman brings the mountain, roughly sargas 101–102)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (the earlier herb flight after Indrajit's weapon, roughly sarga 74)
Tulsidas, Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand (Lakshmana struck; Rama's lament)

notes: Rama's lament ('a wife and kin can be found anywhere, but not a brother like this') is paraphrased from Valmiki Yuddha Kanda (the 'deshe deshe kalatrani' verse, as remembered) and Tulsidas; not quoted. Confirm, and confirm the framing that it is grief, not a ranking of love.

Which weapon struck Lakshmana differs: in Valmiki, Ravana's shakti (spear); in Tulsidas and popular tellings often Meghanada/Indrajit's shakti. The script says 'in Valmiki's telling it's a great spear flung by Ravana himself'. Confirm.
Valmiki has two herb flights (after Indrajit's brahmastra, with Jambavan's guidance; and after Ravana's spear, with Sushena). Confirm the trapdoor wording.
Hanuman worship on Tuesdays and Saturdays (howItsDone) varies by region; confirm.
